exposure: Uterine artery (UtA) Doppler velocimetry during peak uterine contraction (UtA-PI)
outcome: preterm delivery (within 48 hours, 7 days, 14 days, or <=35 weeks, <=37 weeks gestation)
cohort: 172 pregnant women admitted with threatened preterm labor between 24 and 35 weeks' gestation.
finding: Uterine artery pulsatility index (UtA-PI) during peak uterine contractions was significantly higher in patients who delivered within 7 days and was identified as an effective predictor of preterm delivery, alongside cervical length.
gest_age: 24-35 weeks at admission; outcomes assessed for delivery ≤35 weeks and ≤37 weeks
